records.title: How do I apply for SNAP benefits?
records.summary: Apply online through Delaware ASSIST, by mail, or in person at a State Service Center.
records.question: How do I apply for SNAP benefits?
records.answer: Apply online at Delaware ASSIST (assist.dhss.delaware.gov), by mail, or in person at any Division of Social Services State Service Center. You'll need proof of identity, income, and household expenses.

records.title: What is the eviction notice period in Delaware?
records.summary: 5 days for nonpayment of rent, 7 days for lease violations, 60 days for no-cause termination.
records.question: What is the eviction notice period in Delaware?
records.answer: It depends on the reason: 5 days' notice for nonpayment of rent, 7 days for lease violations, and 60 days to end a month-to-month or year-to-year tenancy without cause. Only a court can actually order you to leave.

records.title: Where can I get free legal help in Wilmington?
records.summary: Delaware Volunteer Legal Services and Community Legal Aid Society both offer free civil legal help.
records.question: Where can I get free legal help in Wilmington?
records.answer: Delaware Volunteer Legal Services (302-478-8850) and Community Legal Aid Society (302-575-0660) both provide free civil legal assistance to income-eligible Delaware residents, including housing, employment, and family law matters.

records.title: Am I eligible for LIHEAP heating assistance?
records.summary: Eligibility is based on household size and income, generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level.
records.question: Am I eligible for LIHEAP heating assistance?
records.answer: Eligibility is based on household size and income, generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level. Applications open each fall through your local State Service Center — apply early, as funds are limited.

records.title: What documents do I need to apply for Medicaid?
records.summary: Proof of identity, income, residency, and household size.
records.question: What documents do I need to apply for Medicaid?
records.answer: You'll typically need proof of identity (ID or driver's license), proof of income (pay stubs or a benefits letter), proof of Delaware residency, and information about everyone in your household. You can apply anytime through Delaware ASSIST.

records.title: How do I file an unemployment claim in Delaware?
records.summary: File online through the Delaware Division of Unemployment Insurance as soon as you lose your job.
records.question: How do I file an unemployment claim in Delaware?
records.answer: File online at the Delaware Division of Unemployment Insurance website as soon as possible after losing your job — benefits are not retroactive before your claim date. You'll need your employment history for the past 18 months and your Social Security number.
